findings.title: Potential sensitive logging
findings.explanation: A direct console call receives an argument whose name suggests sensitive data. Current-files mode has no baseline; this is not a confirmed leak.
limitations: Names alone cannot establish sensitive data flow or a confirmed leak.
Only direct console calls and direct named arguments are inspected; aliases, nested objects, computed calls and general access control are not analyzed.
The global console binding is assumed; shadowed bindings can produce false positives.
Static analysis only; no runtime verification occurred.

findings.title: Potential authorization-header logging
findings.explanation: An authorization-header-shaped read reaches a direct console call through supported assignments and directly resolved same-file helper calls. This is a potential exposure, not a verified runtime leak.
limitations: Deterministic straight-line analysis with bounded, directly resolved same-file helpers; no runtime verification.
Header-shaped reads are treated as potential authorization values; receiver types and actual sensitive contents are not proven.
Only direct same-file helper calls are traced (maximum depth 3). No imported helpers, closures, dynamic dispatch, returned-value propagation or general workflow understanding.
Console is assumed to be the standard logger; custom implementations and runtime reachability are not verified.
Current-files review: no baseline comparison; newness is not applicable.
